strategic_capability_mapping.relationship: Existing product completion and product-continuation admission can now preserve bounded unresolved technical-debt continuity from a continue_development decision into the admitted continuation task.
Rust validates bounded debt items, rejects malformed or duplicate carry-forward evidence, and binds replay identity to the resulting SHA-256 fingerprint.

Only bounded debt ids, summaries, milestone/phase/PR references, statuses, next actions, and fingerprints are stored; raw prompts, provider output, file content, diffs, commands, paths, and secrets remain excluded.
Existing task provenance exposes which unresolved debt carried from the source product decision into the next continuation task without adding a separate report surface.

answers.strategic_capabilities: Advances headless_autonomous_development with supporting runtime_permission_enforcement, context_management, and progress_visualization.
answers.new_capability: A continue_development product decision can attach bounded unresolved technical-debt carry-forward items that Rust fingerprints, records in the product-decision ledger payload, and carries into product-continuation provenance.
answers.why_existing_functionality_is_insufficie: Before M54.1, product completion only had technical_debt_reviewed and remaining_capability; it could prove a review happened but could not preserve which debt remained active.
answers.product_gap_if_skipped: Unresolved capability debt can silently disappear between closeout, continuation admission, and the next phase plan because only external prose memory names the debt.
answers.non_duplicative: Distinct from M53.1 admission, M53.1.1 request binding, and M53.2 task.run freshness because it adds a new bounded provenance dimension rather than another continuation route.
answers.no_new_rpc: Yes. The phase extends existing product completion decision and product-continuation admission shapes only.
answers.no_new_summary: Yes. It adds no report, digest, history, readiness, verdict, inspection, preview, dashboard, or standalone summary surface.
answers.runtime_behavior_change: Rust now validates, sorts, fingerprints, persists, replays, and carries technical-debt continuity evidence through existing product-decision and continuation-task paths.
answers.headless_autonomous_contribution: A headless caller can recover active debt obligations from runtime-owned continuation provenance instead of external controller notes.
answers.milestone_progress: This establishes the first M54 primitive required before a later planning gate can enforce carried debt handling.

guard_engine_change_review.review_intent: M54.1 updates the current and archived phase manifests for a runtime-owned technical-debt carry-forward behavior change. Review must confirm guard enforcement is not weakened and no report-only debt registry was added.

exit_criteria: Product completion decision request/result accepts optional bounded technical_debt_carry_forward items without adding a new RPC
Rust validates item count, duplicate debt ids, bounded ASCII metadata, optional PR reference, and raw-field exclusion before ledger mutation
Rust derives a deterministic technical_debt_carry_forward_fingerprint from canonical sorted items
The product-decision ledger payload persists only bounded carry-forward metadata and the fingerprint
Exact replay with matching carry-forward evidence is duplicate-free
Conflicting carry-forward evidence for the same persisted product decision is denied
Product-complete decisions without carry-forward evidence remain valid
Product-continuation admission copies the carry-forward fingerprint and bounded item summaries into ProductContinuationProvenance
VSIX protocol validation accepts the bounded carry-forward shape and rejects malformed or raw debt payloads
behavior_evidence: Rust behavior test headless_run_drive_records_product_completion_decision_and_replays validates bounded carry-forward decision recording, fingerprint exposure, replay stability, and conflicting carry-forward denial.
Rust behavior test task_start_admits_product_continuation_and_replays_without_running validates carry-forward provenance is copied into the admitted continuation task.
VSIX protocol tests validate accepted and rejected technical_debt_carry_forward request/result/provenance payloads.

accepted_capability: Existing product completion and product-continuation admission now carry runtime-owned unresolved technical-debt continuity provenance.
safety_boundary: No new JSON-RPC method or standalone debt report surface
Carry-forward evidence is optional and only bounded metadata is persisted
Duplicate, malformed, non-ASCII, oversized, or raw-looking debt items fail before ledger mutation
Replay identity includes the carry-forward fingerprint
No provider, verifier, apply, shell, git, network, service, automatic run, or workspace mutation capability is added
non_goals: No report, digest, history, readiness, verdict, inspection, preview, dashboard, or summary-only wrapper
No automatic planning, scheduling, task run, provider call, verification, proposal apply, shell, git, network, service, or workspace mutation

No raw issue bodies, review comments, prompts, provider responses, final responses, file content, diffs, stdout/stderr, commands, environment, raw requests, raw ledger payloads, absolute paths, canonical paths, or secrets
No attempt to resolve carried debt in this phase
rejected_alternatives: A standalone debt report endpoint was rejected because it would be report-only and outside the execution/admission path.
A broad technical-debt registry was rejected because M54.1 needs one bounded product-decision-to-continuation vertical slice.
Controller-only review-memory updates were rejected because they are not Rust-owned or replay-safe.
technical_debt: A later M54 phase should enforce how carried debt is addressed, deferred, or superseded during planning.
crates/brownie-runtime/src/lib.rs remains large and should be split only by a future move-only refactor.
next_capability_rationale: M54.2 should use carried technical-debt provenance to constrain planning review rather than adding another passive inspection surface.
